rejectedRevisions.reason: The harness requested a ps output field format that Docker top did not accept; no custody claim was promoted.

architectureInvariants: The provider runs non-root with zero effective capabilities, no-new-privileges, read-only root, seccomp, AppArmor, and explicit PID, memory, and CPU limits.
A trusted worker supervisor owns the complete container/cgroup lifecycle; process-group custody alone is insufficient.
Tenant-controlled code never receives the Docker socket or daemon API.
A Docker bridge is a connectivity boundary, not an endpoint allowlist: every attached peer exposes all listening ports to other peers.
Provider containers attach only to a per-operation egress gateway network; the gateway enforces the signed host, port, protocol, DNS, and byte/time budget.
No provider, database, broker, control plane, or sibling worker shares the provider-facing bridge unless explicitly required and authorized.

remainingGates: OpenCode end-to-end regression in the accepted container boundary
external TLS and DNS egress gateway allowlist conformance
Docker daemon socket protection and trusted-supervisor authorization
custom seccomp and AppArmor policy plus image-signature enforcement
kernel, distribution, Docker, and cgroup-version support matrix
physical power loss and worker-host replacement recovery
